messages.author: 7c31dd3eaed5edbe
messages.subject: Interactions in mixed-effects model
parts:
Hello Rists. I know mixed-effects models are not discussed in Stefan's
book, but I'm wondering if he or anyone else has heard of running main
predictors and their pairwise interactions, as discussed in Stefan's
book (VAR1 + VAR2 + VAR3)^2, in a mixed-effects model with lmer() in
the lme4 package? I just tried it by simply enclosing my fixed effect
variables in parentheses and adding "^2", like in my example above,
but I got an error message:

lmer(S.DUR ~ (LOC.NEW + WL + log(form.freq.2+1) + log(lemma.freq.2+1)
+ pre.phon.factor + fol.letter + pho.str.let + syl.pos.let +
wd.pos.five)^2 + (1|INFORMANT) + (1|tolower(cali.s$word)),
data=cali.s)

Error in mer_finalize(ans) : Downdated X'X is not positive definite,
48.

Does this mean that it's not possible to run pairwise interactions
when running a mixed-effects model? Only linear or logistic
regression, with lm() or glm(), can handle pairwise interactions?

Thanks. Earl Brown

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Interactions in mixed-effects model
parts:
Nah, using ()^x is definitely possible; the problem must be your data
or something else in your model:

library(lme4); set.seed(1)

f1 <- factor(sample(letters[1:3], 1000, replace=TRUE))
f2 <- factor(sample(letters[4:5], 1000, replace=TRUE))
f3 <- factor(sample(letters[6:8], 1000, replace=TRUE))
su <- factor(sample(letters[24:26], 1000, replace=TRUE))
y <- runif(1000)

m <- lmer(y ~ f1 + f2 + f3 + f1:f2 + f1:f3 + f2:f3 + (1|su))
n <- lmer(y ~ (f1 + f2 + f3)^2 + (1|su))
print(m, cor=FALSE) # works
print(n, cor=FALSE) # works, too

STG

Stefan Th. Gries
